truth_yaml_said.x-truth-note: Live returns binary PDF. userLocale (String) is a REQUIRED query param (400 without it). Confirmed endpoint exists — raw GET tool gets JSON parse error on %PDF binary output.
truth_yaml_said.userLocale_description: Required locale string for PDF rendering (e.g. 'en')

probe_1_without_userLocale.error_message: Required request parameter 'userLocale' for method parameter type String is not present

probe_2_with_userLocale_en.error_message: invalid character '%' looking for beginning of value
probe_2_with_userLocale_en.interpretation: HTTP 200 with binary PDF body — raw GET tool fails to JSON-parse the %PDF... response, confirming binary content-type. TRUTH.yaml notes this exact behavior.

probe_3_typed_tool_without_user_locale.finding: Typed tool silently defaults user_locale to 'en-US' when omitted. This default is NOT documented in TRUTH.yaml. The underlying API requires the param (probe_1 confirms 400 without it), so the typed tool layer is masking the requirement.

secondary_finding.finding: The typed tool clockify_invoices_export silently defaults user_locale to 'en-US' when the caller omits it. TRUTH.yaml documents userLocale as REQUIRED at the API level (correctly confirmed by 400 probe), but does not note the tool-layer default. This means the tool's parameter is effectively optional from the MCP caller's perspective, while the raw API requires it. TRUTH.yaml is accurate about the raw API contract; the tool-layer default is unrelated to the spec.
secondary_finding.tool_behavior_note: Add x-tool-note: user_locale defaults to en-US in clockify_invoices_export

notes: Three sub-probes: (1) bare GET without userLocale → 400 confirms TRUTH.yaml required claim; (2) GET with userLocale=en → %PDF binary causes JSON parse error in raw tool, confirming binary response and TRUTH.yaml note; (3) typed tool without user_locale arg → defaults to en-US and succeeds. All three results consistent with TRUTH.yaml. LIVE-VERIFIED status confirmed.
